pages.markdown: A gust snatched the first lantern from its post. It rolled east and bumped into wet ferns. Rabbit sprang after its bobbing glow, but the wind shoved leaves across the path. The lantern vanished among the dripping roots. “Wait there!” Rabbit called to the storm. A crack of thunder answered.

The rain softened to a patter. Lanterns two, three, and four were loose somewhere in the woods. At the woodland edge, the neighbors waited with their picnic baskets. Dark clouds covered the last pink strip of sky. “We need the lights before moonrise,” said Rabbit. “Then everyone can find the glade.”

Rabbit darted east of the first post. Wet fern tips brushed both ears. A small glow winked between the roots. There lay lantern one, muddy but whole. Rabbit grinned and scooped it up. “Found you!” Rabbit said. The true path stretched ahead, and Rabbit hurried on without telling anyone.

Lantern one swung from Rabbit’s paw as Rabbit rushed along the path. The ground forked around a broad stump. One branch curved toward the glade. The other slipped between two thornless bushes. Rabbit barely looked up. “This way!” Rabbit cried, and dashed toward the fork with the lantern.

Rabbit hung lantern one on a low branch beside the side trail. Its glow made the narrow turn look bright and friendly. The true post one stood empty behind the stump. Rabbit leaned back to admire the light. “That should help!” Then Rabbit chased the glow down the wrong branch.

Rabbit raced past a patch of mushrooms, then a crooked root. Soon the same broad stump appeared again. Rabbit had looped back to the fork. The lantern still glowed on the wrong branch. Rabbit’s ears drooped as the sky grew dimmer. “I made this harder,” Rabbit murmured. The neighbors were still waiting.

Wise Turtle came along the main path and stopped at post one. It was empty. Across the fork, lantern one glimmered beside the wrong trail. Turtle had planned to check each post in order. Now Turtle studied the false glow and the wet ground. “One by one may take too long,” Turtle said.

Farther along, Rabbit reached post two. Its hook was bare. A little way east, lantern two rested on a flat stone. Rain shone on its glass. Rabbit stared at it, then looked back toward the fork. The first lantern had landed east of its post, too. Rabbit had another clue to share.

Rabbit lifted lantern two from the flat stone. Rabbit’s paws tingled with the urge to sprint onward. Instead, Rabbit turned toward the fork and called, “Turtle! I found another one east of its post!” The wet trees carried Rabbit’s voice back. Rabbit held still, listening for Turtle’s answer.

Turtle followed Rabbit’s voice along the main path and met Rabbit near post two. Rabbit described the fern roots east of post one, then the flat stone east of post two. Turtle looked from one place to the next on the path. “Both lanterns landed east,” Turtle said. “Let’s use that.”

Turtle traced the path past post three toward the dry creek bend. “If the wind kept pushing east, lantern three may be on that ground,” Turtle said. Turtle pointed farther on, toward the willow ledge for lantern four. The two clues changed the search. Turtle turned away from the empty posts and chose the predicted eastern ground.

Rabbit’s toes tapped against the damp path. A quick dash might find lantern three first. Then Rabbit glanced at the lantern in both paws. “I’ll come with you,” Rabbit said. “The two places match.” Turtle nodded and set a steady pace toward the creek side. Lantern two still needed its post, so Rabbit carried it along.

Rabbit carried lantern two back to post two. Turtle waited beside the post while Rabbit lifted the lantern onto its hook. Its glass caught the last pale light. Rabbit stepped back to make sure it held. Then Rabbit joined Turtle on the path toward post three, leaving both paws free.

East of post three, the path bent toward the dry creek. Turtle let Rabbit scout a few steps ahead, keeping Rabbit in sight. Rabbit checked under broad leaves and beside each tuft of grass. Turtle followed at a calm pace. The creek stones were dry, but the grass nearby still dripped from the storm.

A dim shine showed beneath wet grass. Rabbit found lantern three caught east of post three. Rabbit reached to yank it free, then stopped. The grass pulled tight around its handle. “Wait,” Rabbit said. Turtle eased the blades apart, one at a time. The lantern slipped loose without a crack or scrape.

Rabbit lifted the freed lantern with both paws. Turtle pointed back to post three, and Rabbit carried the light there along the path. The hook gave a small squeak as Rabbit set the lantern in place. Its glow warmed the wet grass. Rabbit checked that it hung straight before walking on with Turtle.

At post four, Turtle looked toward the dry willow ledge. A broad leaf trembled though the air had gone still. Beneath it, a faint glow shone through the dim. “There,” Turtle said. Rabbit followed Turtle’s gaze. Lantern four lay under the leaf, east of its post, where the wind had carried it.

Rabbit did not scoop the lantern up at once. “Where should it go?” Rabbit asked. Turtle pointed to the nearby fourth post. Rabbit lifted lantern four from beneath the leaf and carried it there. The hook held firm. Together they watched its glow join the third lantern’s light.

The three restored lights glowed behind them as Rabbit and Turtle headed back. At the fork, lantern one still hung beside the wrong trail. Its glow lay across the branch like a bright ribbon. Rabbit stopped before it. The neighbors could still be led astray by that tempting light.

Rabbit reached for the wrong-branch lantern, then looked at the dark true post. “I put it here,” Rabbit said. “I’ll fix it.” Rabbit took lantern one down from the branch. The false turn went dark. Turtle waited beside the fork while Rabbit held the lantern close against the evening chill.

Rabbit carried lantern one along the true path toward post one. Turtle walked beside Rabbit, matching Rabbit’s slower steps. At the post, Rabbit lifted the lantern onto its hook. It hung straight and shone over the path. Rabbit let go only after checking that it was secure.

Rabbit and Turtle walked the path together, checking each post. One, two, three, four: every lantern shone in its proper place. The side trail sat dim beside the stump. Beyond the trees, the neighbors still waited at the woodland edge. “The path is ready,” Turtle said. Rabbit turned toward their baskets.

Rabbit hurried to the woodland edge, where the neighbors held their baskets. Rabbit wanted to spring back down the path at once. Instead, Rabbit stopped beside them. “The lights are ready,” Rabbit said. “I’ll go with you.” Wise Turtle stayed beside post one, where the first lantern made a warm pool of gold.

The neighbors picked up their baskets and walked from the woodland edge to post one. Rabbit went with them. Wise Turtle stood beside the first lantern, bright against the dusk. A basket bumped Rabbit’s leg, and bread gave off a warm smell. The group gathered where the true path began.

Wise Turtle pointed along the lit trail from post one. “Follow the lanterns, and keep to this path.” Rabbit looked toward the bright markers, then faced the neighbors. “I’ll lead,” Rabbit said. Turtle stepped in beside the group, leaving the front clear for Rabbit. They set off together at a cheerful pace.

At the fork, Rabbit slowed. Lantern one shone above the true path. The old side branch stayed dark beside the stump. Rabbit led the neighbors along the lighted trail, not toward the tempting turn from before. Turtle walked with them. Basket handles creaked, and no one took the wrong branch.

Rabbit paused beneath lantern two so the neighbors could catch up. Farther on, lantern three glowed beside the creek bend, then lantern four near the willow ledge. Turtle stayed beside the group as baskets swayed along the path. Rabbit kept an easy pace. Each light showed the next stretch clearly.

The trees opened onto the picnic glade. Rabbit led the neighbors inside while the sky still held a strip of pale gold. The moon had not risen. Behind them, all four lanterns shone along the path. Baskets touched the grass, and the neighbors smiled at the tables waiting under the trees.

The neighbors opened their baskets in the glade. Warm bread scented the cool air. Wise Turtle settled beside them, and Rabbit helped pass out cups. The picnic began beneath the trees. Behind the baskets, the lantern path shone through the dusk, while crickets started their evening song.

Rabbit sat beside Wise Turtle and listened to the crickets. The neighbors shared the last warm rolls. Rabbit’s feet still wanted to leap, but Rabbit stayed beside the picnic. Beyond the glade, four lanterns held their places along the path. Their steady glow shone through the trees.
